sections.heading: What NIS2 requires for identities and access
paragraphs: The NIS2 Directive requires essential and important entities to take risk management measures. Three of them concern identities directly: access control policies and asset management, multi-factor authentication, and supply chain security, which includes the access your service providers have.

Each EU member state transposes the directive into national law. In Germany this is the NIS2 Implementation and Cybersecurity Strengthening Act (NIS2UmsuCG), which amends the BSI Act. Management must approve the measures, oversee their implementation and take part in regular training, and it is liable for failures.

In an audit, what counts is what you can show: an approved policy, a complete inventory, recertifications with results, and logs you can actually find when something happens. Having MFA switched on answers none of these questions by itself.

sections.heading: Where identity and access management sits in NIS2
rows: An approved access control policy, an identity inventory, documented granting and removal of access, regular recertification
Access is removed immediately and completely when people leave or change roles
MFA coverage per user group, phishing-resistant methods for administrators and remote access
Supplier access is time-limited, justified, approved and logged
Privileged access management (PAM), IGA for external users
Authentication and change logs that let you reconstruct and report an incident
sections.after: These obligations apply to every account, including service accounts, API keys and AI agents. In many gap analyses, those accounts are the biggest gap.

sections.heading: The NIS2 IAM checklist
sections.intro: We check these eight points in every NIS2 gap analysis. How many can you prove today?

items.title: 1. Access control policy
items.text: Written, versioned and approved by management.

items.title: 2. Complete identity inventory
items.text: Employees, contractors, administrators, service accounts and AI agents, each with an accountable owner.

items.title: 3. Joiner-mover-leaver
items.text: Access is granted and removed automatically when people join, move or leave.

items.title: 4. Recertification with evidence
items.text: Managers and system owners confirm access regularly, and the result is documented.

items.title: 5. MFA for everyone, phishing-resistant for admins
items.text: FIDO2 or passkeys for privileged accounts and remote access.

items.title: 6. Privileged accounts under control
items.text: Vaulted passwords, just-in-time access and session recording for administrators.

items.title: 7. Time-limited supplier access
items.text: Every external access has an end date, a reason and an approval.

items.title: 8. Logs you can find
items.text: Sign-ins and access changes are stored centrally and kept long enough.

sections.heading: How we work
sections.intro: Four steps. After each one, you decide whether and how to continue.

items.title: Gap analysis
items.text: We assess your identities, processes and platforms against the NIS2 requirements and the checklist above. You get a list of gaps, each rated by risk and effort.

items.title: Action plan
items.text: We prioritise the measures by risk and audit relevance, and prepare the documents so your management can approve them.

items.title: Implementation
items.text: We implement the measures on the platform you already run, for example Microsoft Entra ID, One Identity, SailPoint or CyberArk. You see progress in a demo every two weeks.

items.title: Evidence and operations
items.text: We set up reports and recertifications so the evidence is produced as part of daily operations. If you want, we run the platform for you.

items.title: Plain language for management
items.text: We turn articles and clauses into concrete decisions with risk, effort and sequence.

items.title: Vendor-neutral
items.text: We start with what you already license. We recommend a new platform only when the existing one cannot meet the requirements.

items.title: One point of contact
items.text: One dedicated person stays with you from the gap analysis to the audit, in German or English.

items.title: One implementation, several standards
items.text: We map every measure to ISO 27001 (Annex A 5.15 to 5.18 and 8.2) and, where relevant, to DORA.

items.q: Is our organisation covered by NIS2?
items.a: That depends on your sector, your size and your role in the supply chain. National authorities, such as the BSI in Germany, offer self-assessment tools. If you are unsure, we can work it out together in the introductory call.

items.q: Is multi-factor authentication enough for NIS2?
items.a: No. MFA is one of several requirements. Access control, a managed account lifecycle, supplier access and logging are just as much part of it.

items.q: Does NIS2 apply to service accounts and AI agents?
items.a: Yes. The access control requirements apply to every account, human or machine. Technical accounts without an accountable owner are a common audit finding.

items.q: We fall under DORA. Does NIS2 still apply?
items.a: For financial entities, the DORA rules on ICT risk management generally take precedence. The requirements for access control and evidence are very similar, so one implementation can serve both.
Yes, it covers many of the requirements. Check that your scope includes all affected systems and service providers, and that your access controls work in practice.
